extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and other practitioners seeking or advising on USPTO micro entity status
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures to establish and maintain micro entity status under 35 U.S.C. 123 and 37 CFR 1.29, including the gross-income and institution-of-higher-education bases, certification form rules, and related fee/penalty implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that is found to have falsely made a certification under this section shall be subject to a fine, to be determined by the Director, the amount of which shall be not less than 3 times the amount that the entity failed to pay as a result of the false certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies whether the Director discovers the false certification before or after issuance of a patent; fraudulent attempts to establish micro entity status are considered fraud on the Office (see 37 CFR 1.29(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees covered by micro entity discount
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees reduced by 80 percent for micro entities include filing fees (nonprovisional and provisional), search fees, examination fees, issue fees, appeal fees for utility/design/plant/reissue applications, and patent maintenance fees including grace period surcharges and certain surcharge petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes excess claims fees, application size fees, non-DOCX filing surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(u)), surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) when applicable; certain international/PCT and Hague fees have specified effective dates and applicability per CFR references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a written certification
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 123 requires a certification in writing to be filed prior to or at the time a fee is first paid in the micro entity amount in an application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status in one application does not affect other applications; continuation/divisional/CIP/reissue require a new certification (see 37 CFR 1.29(e)); certification may be filed in pending applications, reexamination (for patent owners), supplemental examination, and in patents prior to or concurrent with maintenance fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two statutory bases for micro entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro entity status may be established either on the 'gross income basis' under 35 U.S.C. 123(a) (implemented by 37 CFR 1.29(a)) or the 'institution of higher education basis' under 35 U.S.C. 123(d) (implemented by 37 CFR 1.29(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO forms PTO/SB/15A (gross income basis) and PTO/SB/15B (education basis) implement the respective certifications; no tax returns or notarization required with the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(a)(1) — Small entity requirement (gross income basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must certify that the applicant qualifies as a small entity as defined in § 1.27 without relying on a government use license exception under § 1.27(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every party holding rights in the application must be a small entity; assignment/grant/licensing to a non-small-entity disqualifies the applicant from fee discounts. See MPEP § 509.02 for small entity details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(a)(2) — Application filing limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor has been named as inventor on more than four previously filed patent applications, other than foreign applications, 35 U.S.C. 111(b) provisional applications, or international applications for which the basic national fee under 35 U.S.C. 41(a) was not paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counted applications include previously filed U.S. nonprovisional, reissue, U.S. national stage PCT, and international design Hague applications naming the inventor; previously filed apps are counted regardless of age, pendency, abandonment, or issuance. Non-inventor applicants who are persons also must meet this limit. If all ownership rights in a prior application were assigned due to prior employment, that prior application may be excluded under 37 CFR 1.29(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(a)(3) — Gross income limit on applicants and inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor, in the calendar year preceding the calendar year in which the applicable fee is being paid, had gross income (as defined in 26 U.S.C. 61(a)) exceeding three times the median household income for that preceding calendar year, as most recently reported by the Bureau of the Census.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gross income means total income (not adjusted gross income) and includes compensation, business income, gains, interest, rents, royalties, dividends, pensions, etc. The USPTO posts the 'maximum qualifying gross income' on its website. If prosecution spans calendar years, eligibility must be verified for each preceding calendar year; if the published threshold decreases during a year and a party no longer meets it, a notification of loss (37 CFR 1.29(i)) must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(a)(4) — Gross income limit on parties with ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor has assigned, granted, or conveyed, nor is under an obligation by contract or law to assign, grant, or convey, a license or other ownership interest in the application to an entity that, in the preceding calendar year, had gross income exceeding three times the median household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The gross income limit applies to each assignee, licensee, and any party with an 'ownership interest' regardless of whether the assignee is identified as the applicant. If ownership interest 'has' been transferred (or is obligated to be transferred) to an entity exceeding the limit, micro entity certification cannot be met — this can permanently bar meeting the 1.29(a)(4) certification even if rights are later retransferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate qualification required for each inventor/applicant/owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor and each non-inventor applicant (e.g., assignee-applicant) must separately meet requirements of 37 CFR 1.29(a)(1)-(4) to file a micro entity certification on the gross income basis in the application; parties with ownership interests must also meet the gross income limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any inventor/applicant/owner does not qualify, the application as a whole cannot be certified under the gross income basis. The combined gross income of applicants/inventors is not used; each person is assessed individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(b) — Previously filed application exclusion (employment assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant, inventor, or joint inventor is not considered to be named on a previously filed application for purposes of the application filing limit if the applicant/inventor/joint inventor has assigned, or is under an obligation by contract or law to assign, all ownership rights in the prior application as the result of previous employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify for the exclusion, the assignment/obligation must have resulted from employment with a previous employer (not from the individual's own enterprise).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(c) — Currency conversion for gross income
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant's, inventor's, joint inventor's, or entity's gross income in the preceding calendar year is not in U.S. dollars, the average currency exchange rate as reported by the IRS during that calendar year shall be used to determine whether the gross income exceeds the threshold specified in 1.29(a)(3) or (a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mixed-currency receipts, convert non-USD amounts using the IRS yearly average rate and add to USD amounts to determine qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.29(d) — Institution of higher education basis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish micro entity status under 1.29(d), the applicant must certify that (1) the applicant qualifies as a small entity under § 1.27 (without relying on the government use license exception), and (2) either (i) the applicant's employer (from which the applicant obtains the majority of income) is an institution of higher education as defined in 20 U.S.C. 1001(a), or (ii) the applicant has assigned/granted/conveyed or is obligated to assign/grant/convey a license or other ownership interest in the particular application to such an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office requires small entity status even for 1.29(d) claimants via authority in 35 U.S.C. 123(e). Only a person can claim (d)(2)(i) (since it requires an employer), typically inventors. Attempts to use de minimis transfers to obtain (d) status may be treated as sham transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-sham transaction monitoring for education-basis claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt to obtain micro entity status by merely seeking to transfer a de minimis interest to an institution of higher education could be considered a sham transaction; the Office will monitor claims under 35 U.S.C. 123(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may scrutinize percentage of applicants claiming the education basis to detect improper transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification form content and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO forms PTO/SB/15A (gross income basis) and PTO/SB/15B (education basis) contain the required certifications; no evidence such as a tax return need accompany the form(s), and the form(s) need not be notarized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms must identify the application or patent to which they pertain and be signed by an authorized party per MPEP § 509.04(c). For new filings without application number, providing the first named inventor and title at top of the form is sufficient. Recommended document descriptions: 'Certification of Micro Entity (Gross Income Basis)' and 'Certification of Micro Entity (Education Basis)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and effect of changes in published 'maximum qualifying gross income'
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO posts the applicable 'maximum qualifying gross income' (three times the median household income) on its website and it is anticipated to change (increase or decrease) annually (September/October).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the posted threshold increases, parties who met it earlier in the calendar year remain qualified for that year; if it decreases and a party no longer meets it, a notification of loss of entitlement to micro entity status must be filed and fees cannot be paid at micro entity rates for the remainder of that calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for joint filers, deceased inventors, and legal representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventors who file joint tax returns, gross income for micro entity purposes is the amount the person would report if filing separately (accounting for their portion of joint accounts). Gross income from a deceased inventor's estate/trust does not count toward the gross income limit; however, a legal representative acting as applicant must meet the gross income limit in the preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assignee received all rights and is named as applicant, the assignee must meet the gross income limit instead of the legal representative. All joint inventors, assignees, and licensees must meet the gross income limit to qualify.
